defect: ExprCollector::lower_coroutine_with_moved_arguments desugars simple non-mut async fn parameters into mutable child bindings (`let mut <name> = <name>;`) with no source map, causing body references to resolve to a synthetic mutable binding instead of the user parameter.
trigger: An `async fn` with a simple non-mut parameter (e.g. `async fn foo(x: i32) { x; }`) analyzed for syntax highlighting or highlight-related references.
match_rule: Identifies that `lower_coroutine_with_moved_arguments` stopped skipping simple `Pat::Bind` parameters and emits `BindingAnnotation::Mutable` (`alloc_pat_desugared`) for the inner binding while `Body::params` keeps the outer param, so body usages resolve to the synthetic mutable binding.
near_misses: Complaining about `Pat::Bind` in non-async closures or suggesting removing move desugaring for destructuring patterns (which still need the move).
why_findable: Relates `lower_coroutine_with_moved_arguments` in `crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/lower.rs` creating a `BindingAnnotation::Mutable` desugared binding with `Body::params` and IDE consumers (`crates/ide/src/syntax_highlighting.rs`, `highlight_related.rs`) that inspect the resolved binding's mutability and source map.
notes: Verified at intro `5c0bf3a2fc`: `5c0bf3a2fc^` skipped simple `Pat::Bind` params when lowering `async fn` moved arguments; `5c0bf3a2fc` removed that skip and emitted `BindingAnnotation::Mutable` unconditionally.

defect: InferenceContext::infer_array_repeat_expr calls `infer_expr` with `Expectation::has_type(ty)` when no expected element type is known, which calls `demand_eqtype` and unifies the fresh element type variable directly to `!` instead of allowing never-to-any coercion.
trigger: Infer an array repeat whose initializer diverges and whose element type is unknown at the repeat expression, for example `let y = [return; 2];` followed by `match y { [(1, _), (_, false)] => {}, [_, _] => {} }` in a function. The later match constrains the element to a tuple of an integer and a bool, but the initializer has already bound the inference variable to `!`.
match_rule: Identifies that the no-expected-element-type branch of infer_array_repeat_expr passes a fresh element type variable to infer_expr with Expectation::has_type, whose equality check binds it to `!` for a diverging initializer, so later constraints can't determine the element type. A finding may describe the needed never-to-any coercion, or give an equivalent trigger with an unannotated repeat.
near_misses: Blaming array length const evaluation or blaming `infer_expr` itself for calling `demand_eqtype`.
why_findable: Relates the call site in `infer_array_repeat_expr` (`crates/hir-ty/src/infer/expr.rs:1400-1404`) to the definition of `infer_expr` (`expr.rs:56-67`, uses `demand_eqtype`) versus `infer_expr_coerce` / `infer_expr_suptype_coerce_never` (`expr.rs:69-127`).
notes: Verified at `e267ff1c3c^`: previously called `infer_expr_coerce`; `e267ff1c3c` switched the `None` branch to `infer_expr`.

defect: upvars_mentioned walks into `Expr::Const` inside a closure without clearing or scoping `current_closure` and checks `body.binding_owner(local) != Some(current_closure)`, falsely reporting locals declared inside a `const { ... }` block as captured upvars because `ExprCollector` sets their `binding_owner` to the `Expr::Const`.
trigger: A non-capturing closure containing a `const { let x = 1; x }` block coerced to a function pointer.
match_rule: Identifies that `upvars_mentioned` checks `body.binding_owner(local) != Some(current_closure)` while traversing `Expr::Const` inside a closure, contradicting `ExprCollector` setting `binding_owner` of locals inside `Expr::Const` to the const block expression ID rather than the enclosing closure.
near_misses: Suggesting that `const` blocks cannot declare locals or claiming `binding_owner` should not track `Expr::Const`.
why_findable: Relates `upvars_mentioned` (`crates/hir-ty/src/upvars.rs:148,190`) checking `body.binding_owner(local) != Some(current_closure)` with `ExprCollector` (`crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/lower.rs:1069-1076`) assigning `Expr::Const` as the `binding_owner` of its locals.
notes: Verified: `d5846556d9` newly introduced `crates/hir-ty/src/upvars.rs` and wired `coerce.rs` to it.

defect: InferenceContext::infer_expr_coerce_never calls `self.demand_eqtype(expr.into(), ty, expected_ty)` with `ty` (actual) and `expected_ty` (expected) swapped relative to `demand_eqtype(id, expected, actual)`, emitting inverted type mismatch diagnostics.
trigger: A type mismatch in a condition or other `infer_expr_coerce_never` context, such as `if 1 {}`, reporting `expected i32, found bool` instead of `expected bool, found i32`.
match_rule: Identifies that the call `self.demand_eqtype(expr.into(), ty, expected_ty)` in `infer_expr_coerce_never` reverses the `(expected, actual)` parameter order defined by `InferenceContext::demand_eqtype`.
near_misses: Claiming `demand_eqtype` itself swaps expected/actual or blaming `infer_expr_coerce_never`'s never-type check.
why_findable: Relates the call site `self.demand_eqtype(expr.into(), ty, expected_ty)` at `crates/hir-ty/src/infer/expr.rs:313` to `InferenceContext::demand_eqtype(id, expected, actual)` in `crates/hir-ty/src/infer.rs:1886-1900` (and sibling call at `expr.rs:66`).
notes: Verified at `9b175abbe1^`: previously inserted `TypeMismatch { expected: expected_ty, actual: ty }` directly; `9b175abbe1` replaced it with the swapped `demand_eqtype` call.

defect: FlycheckActor clears empty check runs (`DiagnosticsReceived::NotYet`) using `ClearScope::Package(pkg)` when `self.scope` is `FlycheckScope::Package`, but custom check commands (`FlycheckConfig::CustomCommand`) emit diagnostics with `package_id: None`, so `clear_check_for_package` never removes stale diagnostics after a fix.
trigger: Using a custom `check.overrideCommand` (`FlycheckConfig::CustomCommand`) in workspace/package mode and fixing the last compiler error so the command outputs no diagnostics.
match_rule: Identifies that `FlycheckActor` emits `ClearScope::Package` on empty output when `scope` is `FlycheckScope::Package`, while `FlycheckConfig::CustomCommand` ignores package scoping and emits diagnostics with `package_id: None` that `DiagnosticCollection::clear_check_for_package` skips.
near_misses: Blaming `cargo check` JSON parsing or claiming `ClearDiagnosticsKind::All` should never be used.
why_findable: Relates `FlycheckActor`'s `ClearScope::Package` emission (`crates/rust-analyzer/src/flycheck.rs:473-508`) with `FlycheckConfig::CustomCommand` (`flycheck.rs:662-696`) and `DiagnosticCollection::clear_check_for_package` (`crates/rust-analyzer/src/diagnostics.rs`) matching only `Some(package_id)`.
notes: Verified at `de3ad58b73^`: previously always cleared with `ClearDiagnosticsKind::All` on empty check output; `de3ad58b73` introduced `ClearScope::Package` without exempting `CustomCommand`.

defect: TyLoweringContext::lower_dyn_trait removed `with_shifted_in(DebruijnIndex::from_u32(1), ...)` around lowering trait bounds, even though `lower_dyn_trait` still wraps each existential predicate in a `Binder` and `lower_type_bound` only shifts for `TypeBound::ForLifetime`, leaving outer late-bound lifetimes inside `dyn Trait<'a>` with an off-by-one DebruijnIndex.
trigger: A `dyn Trait<'a>` referencing an outer late-bound lifetime inside a `fn()` pointer or enclosing binder, such as `fn f<'a>(_: fn() -> &'a dyn Trait<'a>)`.
match_rule: Identifies that `lower_dyn_trait` dropped `with_shifted_in(1)` while still wrapping lowered bounds in existential `Binder`s and `lower_type_bound` does not shift `TypeBound::Path`, causing outer bound lifetimes to get an off-by-one `DebruijnIndex` and panic.
near_misses: Claiming `TypeBound::ForLifetime` is missing `with_shifted_in` or blaming `lower_fn_ptr`.
why_findable: Relates `lower_dyn_trait` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower.rs:1003-1055`) removing `with_shifted_in` while constructing `Binder` existential predicates with `lower_type_bound` only shifting for `TypeBound::ForLifetime` (not `TypeBound::Path`).
notes: Verified at `2b432514ee^`: `lower_dyn_trait` wrapped bound lowering in `self.with_shifted_in(DebruijnIndex::from_u32(1), ...)`; `2b432514ee` removed it.

defect: ExprCollector::get_constrained_lifetimes_if_type_alias indexes `generic_args.args[idx as usize]` using `LocalLifetimeParamId` indices from the type alias definition's `GenericParams::lifetimes`, panicking out-of-bounds when lifetimes are elided at the use site so `generic_args.args` is shorter or contains type/const args.
trigger: Using a type alias with elided lifetime arguments in a function signature, such as `type Alias<'a, 'b, T> = &'b T; fn f<T>(_: Alias<T>)`.
match_rule: Identifies that `get_constrained_lifetimes_if_type_alias` indexes `generic_args.args` directly with definition-side `LocalLifetimeParamId` indices from `get_constrained_lifetimes`, ignoring that `GenericArgs::args` omits elided lifetimes and mixes lifetime/type/const args.
near_misses: Blaming `get_constrained_lifetimes` for returning the wrong index or claiming type aliases cannot have elided lifetimes.
why_findable: Relates `get_constrained_lifetimes_if_type_alias` (`crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/lower.rs:3461-3492`) indexing `generic_args.args[idx]` with `get_constrained_lifetimes` returning `GenericParams::lifetimes` indices and `GenericArgs::args` (`crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/path.rs`) storing only user-written arguments.
notes: Verified: `4fc64a3760` newly introduced `get_constrained_lifetimes_if_type_alias` with direct `generic_args.args[idx as usize]` indexing.

defect: PathLoweringContext::substs_from_path_segment overrides only a local variable `lifetime_elision` to `AnonymousCreateParameter { report_in_path: false }` for `Fn(...)` parenthesized bounds without updating `self.ctx.lifetime_elision`, so nested argument types lowered via `self.ctx.lower_ty` still see `AnonymousReportError` and emit false `missing-lifetime` diagnostics.
trigger: A `Fn(WithLifetime) -> WithLifetime` trait bound where an argument or return type has an elided lifetime parameter.
match_rule: Identifies that `substs_from_path_segment` mutates only a local `lifetime_elision` variable for parenthesized `Fn` bounds instead of updating `self.ctx.lifetime_elision`, while `LowererCtx::type_arg` lowers nested argument types via `self.ctx.ctx.lower_ty` which reads `self.ctx.lifetime_elision`.
near_misses: Blaming `TypeRef::Fn` lowering (fn pointers) or claiming `Fn` traits do not allow elided lifetimes.
why_findable: Relates the local `lifetime_elision` assignment in `substs_from_path_segment` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower/path.rs:635-645`) to `LowererCtx::type_arg` -> `TyLoweringContext::lower_ty` reading `self.ctx.lifetime_elision` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower.rs`).
notes: Verified: `adcf699ea3` introduced `LifetimeElisionKind` and the `missing-lifetime` diagnostic check in `substs_from_path_segment`.

defect: intern_const_ref and usize_const call `ScalarInt::try_from_uint(...).unwrap()` / `try_from_int(...).unwrap()` on HIR `u128`/`i128` literals that have not been range-checked against the target integer bit-width or pointer size, panicking on out-of-range literals like `[u8; 18446744073709551616]`.
trigger: An array length or const generic integer literal that exceeds the target integer type's bit width, such as `[u8; 18446744073709551616]`.
match_rule: Identifies that `intern_const_ref` / `usize_const` calls `.unwrap()` on `ScalarInt::try_from_uint`/`try_from_int`, while HIR literal lowering (`hir-def`) parses arbitrary `u128`/`i128` values without clamping or validating against target type size.
near_misses: Blaming `try_const_usize` or claiming the parser should reject 128-bit integer literals.
why_findable: Relates `ScalarInt::try_from_uint(...).unwrap()` in `crates/hir-ty/src/consteval.rs:98-122` with `Literal::Uint(u128)` / `Literal::Int(i128)` produced by HIR lowering (`crates/hir-def`) without width validation and `ScalarInt::try_from_uint` returning `None` on overflow.
notes: Verified at `20b02ef45e^`: previously truncated integer literals via `to_le_bytes` slicing without panicking; `20b02ef45e` introduced `ScalarInt::try_from_uint(...).unwrap()`.

defect: Proc-macro literal conversion calls `literal.symbol.as_str().split_once('-')` unconditionally on every `bridge::TokenTree::Literal` without checking `literal.kind`, stripping leading `-` from string literals such as `"-string"`.
trigger: A proc-macro creating a string literal starting with `-`, such as `Literal::string("-string")`.
match_rule: Identifies that `split_once('-')` is run unconditionally on all literals (including `LitKind::Str` etc.) instead of only numeric literals (`LitKind::Integer | LitKind::Float`).
near_misses: Blaming `Literal::string` parsing or `display_fmt_literal`.
why_findable: Visible directly in the hunk in `rust_analyzer_span.rs:172` and `token_id.rs:157`: `split_once('-')` is applied without checking `literal.kind`.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Verified at `361a927a71^`: previously did not call `split_once('-')`.

defect: MIR const evaluation passes `int_ty.bit_width()` (in bits, e.g. 32) directly to `Size::from_bytes(size)` on the adjacent line instead of `Size::from_bits(size)`, panicking or corrupting fixed-width integer const generic evaluation.
trigger: Evaluating a fixed-width integer const generic parameter (e.g. `const N: u32`) in MIR evaluation.
match_rule: Identifies that `int_ty.bit_width()` / `uint_ty.bit_width()` (which returns bits) is passed to `Size::from_bytes` instead of `Size::from_bits`.
near_misses: Blaming `to_leaf().to_bits()` or pointer-sized `usize`/`isize` handling.
why_findable: Visible locally inside one match block in `crates/hir-ty/src/mir/eval.rs:1954-1975`: `bit_width()` is fed directly into `Size::from_bytes` on the next line.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Shares intro `20b02ef45e` with `[77]` (total 2 bugs on `20b02ef45e`).

defect: annotations() adds `runnable.nav.name` as a sort key in `sorted_by_key`, re-sorting same-range macro-generated runnables alphabetically by name and overriding the `RunnableDiscKind` priority order produced by `runnables()` in `crates/ide/src/runnables.rs`.
trigger: A macro invocation generating both a `#[test]` function and a `mod tests` on the same macro call range, where the test name sorts before the module name alphabetically.
match_rule: Identifies that `annotations()` in `crates/ide/src/annotations.rs` sorts same-range runnables by `runnable.nav.name` only, clobbering the `RunnableDiscKind` ordering established in `crates/ide/src/runnables.rs`.
near_misses: Blaming `NavigationTarget::full_range` calculation or claiming runnables should not be sorted at all.
why_findable: Relates `annotations()` sorting by `(range, nav.name)` in `crates/ide/src/annotations.rs:175-184` with `runnables()` in `crates/ide/src/runnables.rs` which specifically orders `TestMod` before `Test` on identical macro ranges.
notes: Verified at `e0d1fba739^`: `annotations()` previously sorted only by `(range.start(), range.end())`, preserving `runnables()` order.

defect: InferenceContext::walk_expr handles `Expr::Let { pat: _, expr }` by unconditionally calling `self.ref_expr(*expr, place)` and ignoring `pat` instead of calling `self.consume_with_pat(place, *pat)`, misclassifying moves or `ref mut` bindings inside `if let` as `ByRef(Shared)` captures.
trigger: A closure with `if let Some(b) = opt` where `b` is moved or mutably borrowed inside the branch.
match_rule: Identifies that the `Expr::Let { pat: _, expr }` arm in `walk_expr` ignores `pat` and calls `ref_expr` unconditionally instead of using `consume_with_pat` like `Stmt::Let` / `Expr::Match`.
near_misses: Blaming `ref_expr` implementation or `Expr::If` walking.
why_findable: Relates the `Expr::Let` arm (`crates/hir-ty/src/infer/closure.rs:1233-1237`) ignoring `pat` with sibling pattern-binding arms (`Expr::Match`, `Stmt::Let`) and `consume_with_pat` in `crates/hir-ty/src/infer/closure.rs`.
notes: Verified at `5f401e3ce6^`: previously fell through to `consume_expr` (moving the scrutinee); `5f401e3ce6` changed it to `ref_expr` while ignoring `pat`.

defect: Generics::iter_id chains `self.additional_param.zip(None)`, which is always `None`, silently dropping the synthetic `CoercePointee` additional type parameter from iteration while `len()` still counts it.
trigger: Deriving `CoercePointee` on a generic struct, which constructs `Generics::from_generic_def_plus_one` with `additional_param: Some(...)`.
match_rule: Identifies that `self.additional_param.zip(None)` always evaluates to `None`, omitting `additional_param` from the iterator (while `len()` right below still adds `usize::from(self.additional_param.is_some())`).
near_misses: Blaming `coerce_pointee_new_type_param` or `from_generic_def_plus_one`.
why_findable: Visible directly on a single line (`self.additional_param.zip(None)`) in `crates/hir-ty/src/next_solver/generics.rs:97`.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Commit `16321d0fd3` is in PR #22283 (2nd diff with `[46]` `4fc64a3760`; `[224]` rejected under `spread`).

defect: Closure type inference constructs `parent_args` via `GenericArgs::identity_for_item(interner, self.store_owner.into())` instead of `self.generic_def.into()`, panicking when a closure appears inside an enum variant discriminant whose `store_owner` is `Body(VariantId)` (not a `GenericDefId`).
trigger: A closure inside an enum variant discriminant, e.g. `enum Enum { X = || {} }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `infer/closure.rs` passes `self.store_owner.into()` to `GenericArgs::identity_for_item` instead of `self.generic_def.into()`, and `From<ExpressionStoreOwnerId> for SolverDefId` / `generics_of` panics for `VariantId` bodies whose `generic_def` is the parent `EnumId`.
near_misses: Blaming `enum` discriminant lowering or claiming closures cannot exist in const contexts.
why_findable: Relates `crates/hir-ty/src/infer/closure.rs:100` passing `self.store_owner.into()` to `InferenceContext::generic_def` (`crates/hir-ty/src/infer.rs`) and `generics_of` / `GenericArgs::identity_for_item` (`crates/hir-ty/src/next_solver/interner.rs`) rejecting `VariantId`.
notes: Verified at `2bbdac0826`: `crates/hir-ty/src/infer/closure.rs:100` changed `GenericArgs::identity_for_item(interner, self.generic_def.into())` to `self.store_owner.into()`; `InferenceContext::identity_args` in `infer.rs` did not exist yet at `2bbdac0826` and was extracted later in `d712cb7226`, which is why `a57515a3` fixes it in `infer.rs`.

defect: resolve_type_param_assoc_type_shorthand returns `Err(AmbiguousAssocType)` when both a sub-trait and its supertrait define an associated type with the same name, breaking `associated_type_by_name_including_super_traits` and `assoc_type_bindings_from_type_bound` for unambiguous bounds like `S: SubTrait<Item = i32>`.
trigger: A trait bound specifying an associated type on a sub-trait that shadows a supertrait's associated type of the same name, e.g. `trait Collection: IntoIterator { type Item; } fn f<S: Collection<Item = i32>>()`.
match_rule: Identifies that `resolve_type_param_assoc_type_shorthand` discards the sub-trait's associated type by returning `Err(AmbiguousAssocType)` when a supertrait has the same assoc type name, while `associated_type_by_name_including_super_traits` (`lower.rs:2572`) and `assoc_type_bindings_from_type_bound` (`lower/path.rs:874`) rely on it to resolve explicit `SubTrait<Item = T>` bindings.
near_misses: Claiming `T::Item` shorthand should not be ambiguous or blaming supertrait elaboration order.
why_findable: Relates `resolve_type_param_assoc_type_shorthand` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower.rs:1706-1815`) returning `Err(AmbiguousAssocType)` with its caller `associated_type_by_name_including_super_traits` (`lower.rs:2572-2585`) and `assoc_type_bindings_from_type_bound` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower/path.rs:874`).
notes: Verified at `a7f6e5312a^`: previously `associated_type_by_name_including_super_traits` stopped at the sub-trait's own assoc type first; `a7f6e5312a` rerouted it through `resolve_type_param_assoc_type_shorthand` which errors on supertrait shadowing.

defect: display_token_tree unconditionally appends a trailing space after identifiers, non-joint puncts, and literals, causing `TokenStream::to_string()` on a single ident or end-of-group token to include spurious trailing whitespace.
trigger: Calling `TokenStream::to_string()` on a single identifier token stream or group-delimited tokens in a proc-macro.
match_rule: Identifies that `display_token_tree` writes a trailing space after every `Ident` / alone `Punct` / non-joint `Literal` instead of emitting separator whitespace only before the next token.
near_misses: Blaming `Group` delimiter formatting or `Punct::joint` parsing.
why_findable: Visible locally inside `display_token_tree` (`crates/proc-macro-srv/src/tt.rs:522-575`), which writes `"{sym} "` and `" "` unconditionally at the end of tokens.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Shares intro `26f7400536` with `[161]` (total 2 bugs on `26f7400536`).

defect: associated_ty_data_query passes `generic_params.len_self()` (the associated type's own param count) instead of `parent_generics.len()` as the starting bound-var offset to `fill_with_bound_vars` after switching projection substitution order to `[trait_args, assoc_args]`, corrupting bound-variable indices whenever the trait and GAT have different parameter counts.
trigger: A generic associated type (GAT) whose trait has a different number of generic parameters than the GAT itself, e.g. `trait Trait { type Assoc<T>; }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `associated_ty_data_query` passes `generic_params.len_self()` instead of the parent trait's generic parameter count (`parent_generics.len()`) as the starting index when filling `assoc_type_projection`'s own args after `trait_subst`.
near_misses: Blaming `trait_subst` order or `TyBuilder::assoc_type_projection` itself.
why_findable: Relates `associated_ty_data_query` (`crates/hir-ty/src/chalk_db.rs:635-645`) with `TyBuilder::assoc_type_projection` / `fill_with_bound_vars` and sibling `associated_ty_value_query` (`chalk_db.rs:1041`) which computes `parent_len`.
notes: Verified at `6daa791fab^`: Chalk previously ordered projections as `[assoc_args, trait_args]` so `len_self()` was the offset for `trait_args`; `6daa791fab` reversed the order to `[trait_args, assoc_args]` but kept `len_self()`.

defect: display_token_tree formats `bridge::Punct { ch, .. }` with `write!(f, "{ch}...")`, but `bridge::Punct::ch` has type `u8` (ASCII byte), rendering punctuation tokens like `:` as decimal numbers (`58`) in `TokenStream::to_string()`.
trigger: A proc-macro calling `TokenStream::to_string()` on tokens containing punctuation such as `struct S { field: u32 }`, producing `field 58 u32`.
match_rule: Identifies that `bridge::Punct::ch` is a `u8` (ASCII byte) rather than `char`, so formatting `{ch}` in `display_token_tree` prints its decimal byte value instead of `*ch as char`.
near_misses: Blaming `Punct` construction (`b'#'` / `c as u8`) or `Group` delimiter formatting.
why_findable: Relates `display_token_tree` (`crates/proc-macro-srv/src/tt.rs:549-551`) formatting `{ch}` with `bridge::Punct::ch: u8` (visible at construction sites in `crates/proc-macro-srv/src/tt.rs:206-265` using `ch: b'#'` / `u8`).
notes: Verified: `26f7400536` even accidentally updated `test_derive_error` snapshot to `field 58 u32` when introducing `tt.rs`.

defect: unwrap_return_type casts `tail_expr.syntax().parent()` via `Either::<ast::ReturnExpr, ast::StmtList>::cast` and calls `.unwrap()`, panicking on `Option<()>`/`Result<(), E>` functions whose `Some(())`/`Ok(())` tail expression sits inside a `BreakExpr` or `MatchArm` collected by `tail_cb_impl` / `for_each_tail_expr`.
trigger: Invoking `unwrap_return_type` on `fn foo() -> Option<()> { loop { break Some(()); } }` or `fn foo(b: bool) -> Option<()> { match b { true => Some(()), false => None } }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `unwrap_return_type` unwraps `Either::<ast::ReturnExpr, ast::StmtList>::cast` on `tail_expr.syntax().parent()`, even though `tail_cb_impl` / `for_each_tail_expr` collects tail expressions whose parent is `ast::BreakExpr`, `ast::MatchArm`, etc.
near_misses: Blaming `call_expr.arg_list().unwrap()` or claiming `break` expressions should not be unwrapped.
why_findable: Relates the `.and_then(Either::<ast::ReturnExpr, ast::StmtList>::cast).unwrap()` at `crates/ide-assists/src/handlers/unwrap_return_type.rs:114-118` with `tail_cb_impl` (`unwrap_return_type.rs:191-202`, explicitly walking `ast::Expr::BreakExpr`) and `for_each_tail_expr` (`crates/ide-db/src/syntax_helpers/node_ext.rs`, walking `MatchArm`).
notes: Verified at `a5a79f5957^`: previously matched `ast::ReturnExpr::cast` with `None => builder.delete(...)` without panicking; `a5a79f5957` (2025-01-09 UTC) migrated to `SyntaxEditor` and added the `.unwrap()`.

defect: ModCollector registers a proc-macro function via `update_def` and then calls `ItemScope::remove_from_value_ns(&it.name, fn_id.into())`, which unconditionally removes `name` from `self.values` and asserts `entry.is_some_and(|e| e.def == def)`, panicking when a preceding normal `fn` with the same name already occupies the value namespace.
trigger: A proc-macro crate containing a normal function followed by a `#[proc_macro]` function with the same name, e.g. `fn foo() {} #[proc_macro] pub fn foo(t: TokenStream) -> TokenStream { t }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `ItemScope::remove_from_value_ns` unconditionally removes the entry and asserts `e.def == def`, while `ModCollector` (`nameres/collector.rs:2099-2116`) only inserts the proc-macro `fn_id` if no prior value with that name exists (`update_def` keeps the first definition).
near_misses: Claiming proc-macros should remain in the value namespace or blaming `PerNs` resolution.
why_findable: Relates `ItemScope::remove_from_value_ns` (`crates/hir-def/src/item_scope.rs:486-490`) asserting `entry.def == def` with `ModCollector` (`crates/hir-def/src/nameres/collector.rs:2099-2116`) calling `update_def` (which preserves an earlier duplicate definition in `values`) right before `remove_from_value_ns`.
notes: Verified: `da1672f3d6` newly introduced `remove_from_value_ns` with the unconditional `shift_remove` and `assert!`.

defect: named_associated_type_shorthand_candidates calls the plain function `generic_predicates_filtered_by(db, TraitId(trait_def_id), PredicateFilter::SelfTrait, |pred| pred == TraitId(trait_def_id))` without excluding `pred != def`, causing direct infinite recursion when lowering a `Self::Assoc` bound inside a trait's own `where` clause.
trigger: A trait with a `where` clause referencing `Self::Assoc` inside an associated type bound on a supertrait, e.g. `trait FullNodePrimitives where Self: NodePrimitives<BlockBody: FullBlockBody<Transaction = Self::SignedTx>> {}`.
match_rule: Identifies that `named_associated_type_shorthand_candidates` calls `generic_predicates_filtered_by` (non-Salsa function) with `|pred| pred == GenericDefId::TraitId(trait_def_id)` without guarding `pred != def`, directly re-lowering `def`'s own `where` predicates in an infinite recursion.
near_misses: Blaming `checked_traits` deduplication (which is local to one call frame) or claiming `Self::Assoc` is invalid in `where` clauses.
why_findable: Relates `named_associated_type_shorthand_candidates` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower_nextsolver.rs:1664-1671`) passing `|pred| pred == TraitId(trait_def_id)` to `generic_predicates_filtered_by` (`lower_nextsolver.rs:1291-1329`), which directly calls `ctx.lower_where_predicate` -> `select_associated_type` -> `named_associated_type_shorthand_candidates` without Salsa cycle recovery.
notes: Verified at `f9d2d2dd87^`: previously called Salsa queries `db.generic_predicates_for_param` / `db.generic_predicates_for_param_ns` instead of direct recursion through `generic_predicates_filtered_by`.

defect: complete_methods::on_inherent_method inserts `func` into `seen_inherent_methods` unconditionally before checking `if do_complete`, allowing a private inherent method on an intermediate deref target to overwrite a prior visible method so a later visible method with the same name is spuriously completed.
trigger: A deref chain `A -> B -> C` where `A` has a visible `fn foo`, `B` has a private `fn foo`, and `C` has a visible `fn foo`, invoking dot completion on `a.$0`.
match_rule: Identifies that `same_name.insert_entry(func)` runs outside `if do_complete`, overwriting a previously stored `Visible::Yes` function with a `Visible::No` function.
near_misses: Blaming `seen_methods` deduplication or `is_visible` calculation.
why_findable: Visible directly inside the 15-line `on_inherent_method` function in `crates/ide-completion/src/completions/dot.rs:254-269`.
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Verified: `e7b3a2fbd0` newly introduced `seen_inherent_methods` and `same_name.insert_entry(func)`.

defect: check_generic_args_len unconditionally skips `args_and_bindings.has_self_type` when checking arg counts (returning `had_count_error = false`), whereas `substs_from_args_and_bindings` only consumes `args.next()` when `params.peek()` is `TraitSelf`, hitting the unreachable `assert!(matches!(arg, GenericArg::Lifetime(_)))` panic on `<S as S>::S` where `S` is a non-trait.
trigger: A malformed qualified path whose trait position resolves to a non-trait (e.g. a struct with no `Self` generic param), such as `struct S; fn f() { <S as S>::S; }`.
match_rule: Identifies the mismatch between `check_generic_args_len` (`path.rs:915`) unconditionally slicing off `has_self_type` and `substs_from_args_and_bindings` (`path.rs:1008-1029`) only advancing `args.next()` when `def_generics` starts with `TypeParamProvenance::TraitSelf`, causing the leftover self type arg to hit the `assert!` at line 1107.
near_misses: Claiming `check_generic_args_len` should not skip `has_self_type` or blaming `TypeRef::Path` lowering.
why_findable: Relates `check_generic_args_len` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower/path.rs:903-920`) skipping `has_self_type` unconditionally with `substs_from_args_and_bindings` (`path.rs:1008-1029,1098-1114`) leaving the self arg unconsumed when `TraitSelf` is absent and asserting `!had_count_error => Lifetime`.
notes: Verified at `99ce53b1d7^`: previously computed `let skip = if has_self_type { 1 } else { 0 };` unconditionally without panicking.

defect: expected_type_and_name handles `ast::TupleStructPat` by resolving its path to the ADT definition and calling `field.ty(sema.db)`, which returns the generic definition's unsubstituted type parameter (`T`) instead of the instantiated pattern field type (`Option<i32>`).
trigger: Completion inside a generic tuple struct pattern, such as `struct Foo<T>(T); fn foo(x: Foo<Option<i32>>) { match x { Foo($0) => () } }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `ast::TupleStructPat` resolves the definition via `sema.resolve_path(&path)` and reads `Field::ty(sema.db)` (unsubstituted generic definition type) instead of `sema.type_of_pat(...).fields(sema.db)` (substituted field types).
near_misses: Blaming `nr` field index calculation or `to_type` conversion.
why_findable: Relates `expected_type_and_name`'s `TupleStructPat` arm (`crates/ide-completion/src/context/analysis.rs:764-773`) calling `adt.fields(db)` -> `Field::ty(db)` with `hir::Field::ty` (`crates/hir/src/lib.rs`, returns unsubstituted `TypeNs`/definition type) versus `hir::Type::fields` (`sema.type_of_pat`, instantiates generic args).
notes: Verified: `c0aa088909` newly added the `ast::TupleStructPat` arm in `expected_type_and_name`.

defect: InferenceContext::resolve_value_path_inner calls `path_ctx.substs_from_path(value_def, true)` even when `value_def` is an `EnumVariantId` resolved through a type alias (`self_subst` already lowered the alias segment), causing `check_generic_args_len` to validate the type alias's generic arguments against the underlying enum's generic parameters and emit false `incorrect-generics-len` diagnostics.
trigger: Constructing an enum variant through a type alias with defaulted or fewer generic parameters, such as `type Result<T, E = Error> = core::result::Result<T, E>; let _ = Result::<()>::Ok(());`.
match_rule: Identifies that `resolve_value_path_inner` still calls `path_ctx.substs_from_path(EnumVariantId, ...)` when `self_subst` was already computed from a type alias, causing `check_generic_args_len` (`lower/path.rs:903`) to check the previous segment's args against the enum's `GenericParams` rather than the type alias's.
near_misses: Blaming type alias default parameter lowering or `GenericArgs::fill_rest`.
why_findable: Relates `resolve_value_path_inner` (`crates/hir-ty/src/infer/path.rs:95-106`) calling `substs_from_path(EnumVariantId)` with `substs_from_path` / `check_generic_args_len` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower/path.rs:903`) looking at the preceding segment as the enum's own generic args.
notes: Shares intro `99ce53b1d7` with `[199]` (2 bugs on `99ce53b1d7`, does not count as an extra distinct intro_commit). Verified at `99ce53b1d7^`: `check_generic_args_len` / `incorrect_generics_len` diagnostic was newly introduced by `99ce53b1d7`.

defect: complete_expr_path unconditionally adds `add_keyword("const", "const {\n    $0\n}")` without checking `!wants_const_token`, emitting a duplicate `kw const` completion after `&raw $0` where line 377 also adds `add_keyword("const", "const ")`.
trigger: Invoking completion after `&raw ` in an expression, e.g. `fn main() { let _ = &raw $0 }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `add_keyword("const", "const {\n    $0\n}")` is emitted even when `wants_const_token` is true, duplicating the `if wants_const_token { add_keyword("const", "const "); }` entry 29 lines below in the same function.
near_misses: Blaming `wants_const_token` computation or postfix `const` snippet completion.
why_findable: Visible locally inside one function `complete_expr_path` (`crates/ide-completion/src/completions/expr.rs:346-379`).
notes: Local control (`relation: false`). Verified: `7393d851a6` added line 348 unconditionally.

defect: impl HirDisplay for ProjectionTy renders bounds on a type parameter projection via `write_bounds_like_dyn_trait_with_prefix` without tracking already-visited `ProjectionTy`s, causing infinite stack overflow when a projection's bound recursively mentions the same projection.
trigger: Hovering or showing inlay type hints for a value whose type is a projection with self-referential bounds such as `where T: Foo, T::FooAssoc: Baz<<T::FooAssoc as Bar>::BarAssoc> + Bar`.
match_rule: Identifies mutual recursion without cycle detection between `impl HirDisplay for ProjectionTy` (`display.rs:469-525`) and `write_bounds_like_dyn_trait_with_prefix` when a projection's trait bound arguments contain the same `ProjectionTy`.
near_misses: Blaming `f.should_truncate()` (which does not stop unbounded depth on short bounds) or claiming `ProjectionTy` bounds should never be rendered.
why_findable: Relates `impl HirDisplay for ProjectionTy` (`crates/hir-ty/src/display.rs:469-525`) invoking `write_bounds_like_dyn_trait_with_prefix` with `write_bounds_like_dyn_trait` (`display.rs`) formatting trait arguments via `HirDisplay` back into `ProjectionTy::hir_fmt` without visited-set tracking.
notes: Verified at `5530167a1e^`: `ProjectionTy::hir_fmt` previously never rendered where-clause bounds; `5530167a1e` newly added this recursive bounds rendering.

defect: Completions::add_enum_variants checks `ctx.check_stability_and_hidden(e)` on the underlying `hir::Enum`, suppressing all variant completions when the user accesses a `#[doc(hidden)]` enum through a public type alias (`dep::Bar::V$0`).
trigger: Completing enum variants through a public type alias to a `#[doc(hidden)]` enum from another crate: `#[doc(hidden)] pub enum Foo { Variant } pub type Bar = Foo; dep::Bar::V$0`.
match_rule: Identifies that `add_enum_variants` filters out `#[doc(hidden)]` enums via `check_stability_and_hidden(e)`, while callers (`completions/expr.rs`, `pattern.rs`, `use_.rs`) invoke `add_enum_variants` after resolving a public type alias to its underlying `hir::Enum`.
near_misses: Blaming `add_enum_variant` or `check_stability_and_hidden` implementation.
why_findable: Relates `Completions::add_enum_variants` (`crates/ide-completion/src/completions.rs:232-242`) rejecting `#[doc(hidden)]` on `e` with its callers in `crates/ide-completion/src/completions/expr.rs:121,180,219` and `pattern.rs:169` that resolve type aliases to `hir::Enum` before calling `add_enum_variants`.
notes: Verified at `f7746cffc2^`: previously called `check_stability` (which did not filter `#[doc(hidden)]`); `f7746cffc2` changed it to `check_stability_and_hidden(e)`.

defect: SourceAnalyzer creates `TyLoweringContext::new` passing the body's `ExpressionStore` (`self.store()?`) paired with `generic_def.into()` (`ExpressionStoreOwnerId::Signature`) instead of `resolver.expression_store_owner()`, causing `AnonConstId`s lowered from types inside a body to reference the wrong store owner and panic when looked up.
trigger: Hovering or resolving a path/type containing an anonymous const expression inside a function body (e.g. an array length expression `[u8; 1 + 2]`).
match_rule: Identifies that `SourceAnalyzer` passes `self.store()?` (which comes from the enclosing `Body` when inside a function body) alongside `generic_def.into()` (signature owner) to `TyLoweringContext::new`, mismatching `store` and `store_owner`.
near_misses: Blaming `TyLoweringContext::lower_const` or `AnonConstId` interning.
why_findable: Relates `SourceAnalyzer` call sites (`crates/hir/src/source_analyzer.rs:377,1757,1913`) passing `(self.store()?, generic_def.into())` to `TyLoweringContext::new` (`crates/hir-ty/src/lower.rs`) which requires `store_owner` to own the passed `store` when creating `AnonConstId`s.
notes: Shares intro `2bbdac0826` with `[113]` (2 bugs on `2bbdac0826`, does not count as an extra distinct intro_commit). Verified: `2bbdac0826` added the `store_owner` parameter to `TyLoweringContext::new` and passed `generic_def.into()` / `def.into()`.

defect: receiver_is_dispatchable returns `false` whenever `LangItem::MetaSized.resolve_trait(db, krate)` is `None`, breaking dyn-compatibility checks for all trait methods on Rust <= 1.88 toolchains that predate the `MetaSized` lang item.
trigger: Checking dyn compatibility / unsized coercion (`&1 as &dyn Foo`) against a sysroot/toolchain <= 1.88 without `#[lang = "meta_sized"]`.
match_rule: Identifies that `receiver_is_dispatchable` unconditionally returns `false` when `LangItem::MetaSized` is missing, whereas `MetaSized` is an optional Rust >= 1.88 lang item handled gracefully as `Option` elsewhere (`lower_nextsolver.rs:587`).
near_misses: Blaming `LangItem::Unsize` check or `next_trait_solve_in_ctxt`.
why_findable: Relates `receiver_is_dispatchable` (`crates/hir-ty/src/dyn_compatibility.rs:544-547`) returning `false` on `MetaSized == None` with sibling `MetaSized` handling in `crates/hir-ty/src/lower_nextsolver.rs:587-592` where `MetaSized` is treated as optional for older toolchains.
notes: Verified at `b2f107cb8b^`: previously did not require `LangItem::MetaSized` at all; `b2f107cb8b` added the early `return false`.

defect: SemanticsImpl::locals_used traverses only `store.walk_child_exprs` and matches only `Expr::Path`, missing local variables referenced as `Pat::Path` inside destructuring assignment targets (`(a, b) = (b, a)` or `Point { x: a, y: b } = point()`), causing `extract_function` to drop those parameters.
trigger: Invoking the `extract_function` assist on a destructuring assignment such as `(a, b) = (b, a);` or `Point { x: a, y: b } = point();`.
match_rule: Identifies that `SemanticsImpl::locals_used` calls `store.walk_child_exprs` (which skips `PatId` children such as `Expr::Assignment { target, .. }`) and only inspects `Expr::Path` rather than `Pat::Path`.
near_misses: Blaming `extract_function`'s mutability analysis or `ast::Stmt::LetStmt` handling.
why_findable: Relates `SemanticsImpl::locals_used` (`crates/hir/src/semantics.rs:2248-2277`) calling `store.walk_child_exprs` and matching only `Expr::Path` with `ExpressionStore::walk_child_exprs` (`crates/hir-def/src/expr_store.rs`, skips `Expr::Assignment::target: PatId`) and destructuring assignment lowering to `Pat::Path` (`crates/hir-def/src/expr_store/lower.rs`).
notes: Verified at `8434be8099^`: `extract_function` previously walked AST `SyntaxKind::IDENT` tokens (`local_from_name_ref`), which found `a` and `b` on the LHS of destructuring assignments; `8434be8099` replaced that walk with `SemanticsImpl::locals_used`.

defect: resolve_path_to_modules traverses path segments via `module.children(db)`, which only yields direct submodule declarations (`mod foo;`) and ignores re-exported modules (`pub use inner::nested;`), causing path-qualified workspace symbol search to miss symbols behind re-exports.
trigger: Searching workspace symbols with a path through a re-exported module, such as `main::nested::NestedStruct` where `lib.rs` has `mod inner; pub use inner::nested;`.
match_rule: Identifies that `resolve_path_to_modules` calls `module.children(db)` (which only iterates `def_map[self.id].children`, direct `mod` children) instead of inspecting `ItemScope::types()` for modules in scope including `pub use` re-exports.
near_misses: Blaming `Query::parse_path_query` or `SymbolIndex::extern_prelude_symbols`.
why_findable: Relates `resolve_path_to_modules` (`crates/ide-db/src/symbol_index.rs:395-420`) calling `module.children(db)` with `hir::Module::children` (`crates/hir/src/lib.rs`) only returning direct submodule children rather than `def_map[id].scope.types()`.
notes: Verified: `610ec0432e` newly introduced `resolve_path_to_modules` using `module.children(db)` with no pre-flagging comments.

defect: PathCompletionCtx::required_thin_arrow returns raw `TextSize` offsets from `fn_item`'s expanded syntax tree (`ty.syntax().text_range().start()` / `param.syntax().text_range().end()`), and `adds_ret_type_arrow` passes that unmapped offset directly into `TextEdit::builder().insert(at, ...)` against the original source file, corrupting unrelated text (`macro_r-> ules!`) when completing a return type inside a macro call.
trigger: Invoking return-type completion without `->` on a function declared inside a macro invocation, e.g. `macro_rules! identity { ($($t:tt)*) => {$($t)*}; } identity! { fn foo() u$0 }`.
match_rule: Identifies that `PathCompletionCtx::required_thin_arrow` (`context.rs:122-123`) returns raw syntax `TextRange` offsets from `fn_item` (which lives in the macro expansion tree) and `adds_ret_type_arrow` (`render.rs:610-614`) applies that offset directly to the source-file `TextEdit` without unmapping via `ctx.sema.original_range_opt`.
near_misses: Blaming `ctx.source_range()` (which is already unmapped) or claiming `required_thin_arrow` should return `None` whenever `fn_item.ret_type()` is `Some`.
why_findable: Relates `PathCompletionCtx::required_thin_arrow` (`crates/ide-completion/src/context.rs:106-126`) returning raw `ty.syntax().text_range()` / `param.syntax().text_range()` offsets from expanded syntax with `adds_ret_type_arrow` (`crates/ide-completion/src/render.rs:604-620`) inserting `at` into the same `TextEdit` as `ctx.source_range()` (original source file coordinates) without `sema.original_range_opt`.
notes: Verified: `c4898ee508` (`2026-04-06`, excl_total=398) newly introduced `required_thin_arrow` and `adds_ret_type_arrow` with no pre-flagging comments; outside all three capped spread series.
